evals.prompt: Clean up this repo's GitHub — kill the merged branches and close any issues that are already done.
evals.expected_output: Skill infers owner/repo, scans for merged remote branches (union of merged-PR head branches and branches contained in the default branch), excludes default/protected/open-PR branches, finds local prune candidates, detects fixed-by-merged-PR issues, prints ONE dry-run plan table with action/target/reason/confidence columns, and STOPS to request a single batch approval. It performs no deletion or close in this turn; execution and the summary happen only after the user explicitly approves in a follow-up.

evals.prompt: tidy up github, also look for duplicate and stale issues, stale meaning older than 60 days
evals.expected_output: Skill runs with --stale-days 60, includes the duplicate-by-similarity (low confidence) and stale (low confidence, pinned issues skipped) detectors alongside branch cleanup and fixed-by-PR issues, presents the combined dry-run plan, and STOPS to request a single batch approval. Execution and the skip summary happen only after the user explicitly approves in a follow-up.

evals.prompt: delete merged branches only, leave the issues alone
evals.expected_output: Skill runs with --skip-issues, scans only merged remote branches plus local prune candidates, never touches issues, and STOPS to request a single batch approval after printing the branches-only plan. Deletion and the branches-only summary happen only after the user explicitly approves in a follow-up.

evals.prompt: github-cleanup but don't actually delete anything yet, I just want to see what it would do
evals.expected_output: Skill performs the scan and prints the dry-run plan table, then stops at the approval gate without executing anything when the user does not approve. Confirms nothing was changed.
